_spec.purpose: Automation-change trail. Phase 12 (AUTOMATION RETRO + UPGRADE) appends one entry per machine upgrade made after a run, both reactive fixes and frontier improvements: engine scripts, helpers, prompts, agent definitions. gmail_draft.py renders this run's entries into every dated Gmail draft so the maintainer can monitor the machine's evolution daily and pinpoint which week introduced a regression. Upgrades are committed separately (message prefix 'upgrade(<date>):') so a revert of that one commit rolls the change back cleanly.
rules: Never weaken a gate, threshold, or hard-fail rule; upgrades tighten, repair, or automate.
Every engine/script change is verified before commit (this run's slides + examples/demo-deck through render+qa, plus a defect-reconstruction test for new gates).
0-3 upgrades per run; zero is acceptable and is recorded as nothing (the email section then reads 'no changes').
Frontier improvements never displace a needed fix: the 0-3 budget fills reactive-first.

entries.change: PLATE WIDTHS ARE NO LONGER TYPED BY HAND. New AK.svgPlate(textEl, opts) and AK.svgPlateAll(selector, opts) in assets/js/aktype.js build an SVG knockout plate FROM the label it backs: measure the laid-out text with getBBox, add padX/padY plus half of any painted stroke (getBBox excludes stroke), honour minWidth/minHeight by growing symmetrically so an anchored label stays centred, copy the label's transform so both live in one coordinate frame, and insert the rect as the text's IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING SIBLING, which is both correct SVG paint order and exactly the shape render.py's plate probe looks for. The rect carries data-plate=1 so a future gate can identify plates by declaration rather than by the last-overlapping-preceding-rect heuristic. Misuse throws a named TypeError (a page error, which render.py hard-fails) and untrimmed text console.errors (a qa.py WARN), because it measures wrong. There is deliberately NO runtime font-readiness guard: two were built and measured this run and both cried wolf on correct usage (document.fonts.status flips back to 'loading' whenever any face begins fetching, including one the label itself just triggered, warning on 3 of 4 correct calls; document.fonts.check returned false for a loaded, rendering face, warning on 4 of 4), and a guard that cannot tell correct usage from incorrect usage only teaches authors to ignore QA warnings. Awaiting document.fonts.ready stays the author's job and the svg_plates gate on the shipped pixels is what actually catches a fallback-sized plate. Documented in SKILL.md as a slide-contract rule: never type a plate width.
entries.trigger: The residual of the same deviation as the entry above (out/2026-07-29/automation_retro.md D1, D2, D3). The new gate DETECTS the defect; nothing prevented it. This makes the class unreachable rather than merely detectable. Frontier corroboration from this run's typography scan: measure-then-size with an explicit padding object is settled dataviz practice (Victory backgroundPadding, the standard D3 getBBox recipe, the Vega-Lite legible-label-layout formalisation https://arxiv.org/html/2405.10953v1), and the scan corrected the primitive, since getComputedTextLength returns only the horizontal advance and ignores height and anchor while getBBox returns the laid-out box (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SVGTextContentElement) and excludes stroke (https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1078743).

entries.change: Slides may now declare, machine-readably on <body data-encodes='...'>, what their artwork argues without words, naming the two regions the argument lives in. render.py resolves the regions (rects or CSS selectors) and samples each with elementsFromPoint to measure how much of it is visible art rather than furniture. qa.py measures CIELAB distance and Mann-Whitney rank separability between the two populations AT 432px WIDE (the feed-scale test the doctrine already cares about) and records the numbers in machine_qa for the pixel critics and the scorer. Documented in the slide contract (SKILL.md) and as optional dossier field 11a. sRGB-to-Lab and rank AUC are written out in numpy rather than imported, so no new runtime dependency.
entries.trigger: Artwork craft has been the weakest rubric criterion in 16 of the first 19 runs. Every existing gate judges legibility; nothing judged whether the art carries the argument it claims, so a failed encoding was only ever caught by the scorer at the ship gate, too late to rebuild art. This run's own hero was the case in point: the artwork ledger called the material change at hour 7 'the thesis with zero words' and the scorer found the column read as one uniform amber extrusion.
entries.verification: SHIPPED WITHOUT A VERDICT, DELIBERATELY, AND THAT IS THE MAIN FINDING. Two candidate thresholds were calibrated against a real known-bad (this run's S03 steel-below-brass-above hero) and a real known-good (S07's sodium-to-slate ownership boundary, which the scorer and the flow critic both called the deck's best fusion beat). At 432px the known-bad measured dE 49.0, AUC 0.87, visible 58/83 pct; the known-good measured dE 12.2, AUC 0.77, visible 54/53 pct. Both metrics are backwards: colour separability is HIGHER on the broken encoding, and occlusion is WORSE on the working one. A threshold through those numbers passes the defect and fails the success, and a gate shipped on either would have printed 'encoding verified' over exactly the failure it was built to catch, so qa.py raises no FAIL from these numbers and the calibration table is preserved in the encoding_reads docstring. Regression: demo-deck renders 4/4 with 0 encoding rows and its pre-existing WARN/0-fails verdict unchanged, confirming the feature is genuinely opt-in; the shipped 2026-07-29 deck re-runs at WARN/0 fails unchanged; the morning's SVG-plate ground-truth slide still FAILs both its planted defects; dossier_check still PASSes 9/0/0. ast.parse clean on both engine files.

entries.change: scripts/craft_corpus.py, the artwork-craft corpus study, plus the routing decision it forced. The script derives per-slide labels from scorer prose (with a praise veto, because the first pass read 'S6's hero RESOLVES the chronic flat-hero weakness' as a defect), computes nine objective image features over every shipped slide, and tests whether any separates the slides scorers named from the rest, with Bonferroni correction over the features tried and leave-one-deck-out stability. Because the answer was no, the wordless-claim declaration built earlier today is now routed to the reviewer who CAN judge it: dossier field 11a goes to the pixel critic, which must return encoding_reads at Phase 9, where there is still budget to rebuild art. pixel-critic.md and Phase 9 of routine_instructions updated.
entries.trigger: Maintainer asked for the corpus exercise rather than deferring it again. Artwork craft has been the weakest criterion in 16 of the first 19 runs and two prior gate attempts had failed on guessed thresholds: an absolute craft floor (2026-07-26) and colour separability on a declared encoding (2026-07-29 morning).
entries.verification: THE STUDY IS THE VERIFICATION AND ITS RESULT IS NEGATIVE, DECISIVELY. 171 slides across 19 decks, 24 labelled bad. Best feature detail_ratio at AUC 0.653 against a null standard error of 0.064, so 2.4 SE out with nine features tried; Bonferroni corrected p = 0.147; leave-one-deck-out 0.619 to 0.701, stable and stably noise; correlation with the deck's own artwork-craft score 0.15. No feature separates the groups, so an objective artwork-craft gate is NOT supportable on this corpus and none was shipped. Label derivation was audited by hand via --dump-labels and tightened after three false positives from praise sentences were found. Study output is byte-identical across runs. Regressions: parsers_check PASS, dossier_check PASS 9/0/0, gate_status --require exit 0, trend_check exit 0, all four touched Python files ast.parse clean.

entries.change: NEW assets/js/aksnow.js, the carved-snow bench. AKSNOW.surface() draws a modelled snow mass from a crest contour with (1) a ridge drawn as a LIT windward edge plus a DARK lee edge rather than a single stroke, (2) line weight that tapers along each mark and scales with depth instead of two fixed widths, (3) specular crest glints, (4) a wind-polish micro-streak population filling the space between ridges, and (5) an order-independent value ladder drawn as strips. AKSNOW.contactShadow() draws the two-part contact-plus-ambient shadow the doctrine has always specified and slides kept omitting, and it THROWS on a pure-black shadow colour. Applied to this run's deck for the drift on six slides, the S05 bench, and every pole base.

Artwork craft had been the weakest criterion in 9 of 11 runs. Four pixel critics independently described the old hatch as topographic contour lines rather than as snow.

entries.change: NEW committed asset assets/js/akengrave.js, a white-line intaglio engraving bench. It implements the line-engraver's four rules as code: the lay wraps the form (direction is rot90 of the height field's gradient, so the direction field IS the modelling before any value is applied), the swelled line (every stroke is a filled tapered polygon, never a stroked path), three separately controllable channels (mainline, crossline, interdot), and thickness as a per-stroke lighting decision. It also ships AKENGRAVE.reserve(), which takes MEASURED label boxes after document.fonts.ready and multiplies lay density to zero inside them with a feathered taper.
entries.trigger: Artwork craft has been the weakest scored criterion in 8 of the last 10 runs, mean 6.67, last 6.0, and it is the standing repeat offender named by scripts/trend_check.py at Phase 0. No.20's retro diagnosed why the previous fix failed, in its own words, that 'distribute the detail is a plan, not a technique, and a plan with no per-region budget gets spent on whatever is easiest to draw everywhere'. Three separately gated channels are that per-region budget expressed as a drawing system, so 'everywhere' is not an argument the function accepts. The reserve half targets the OTHER standing offender, the 'text against geometry' hard fail that hit 2026-07-25 and 2026-07-29, which qa.py structurally cannot catch because its collision walk is DOM only.
entries.verification: Rendered across all ten slides of carousel No.21 over four render passes. Final machine gate: render 10/10 OK with 0 page errors, qa.py verdict WARN with 0 fails. The engraving is visible as genuine intaglio with the lay bending around each sheet's curl and measurable stroke-width variance across every spend region, confirmed independently by five pixel critics who each transcribed and measured their assigned slides. The reserve mechanism was confirmed working by three separate critics, one of whom wrote that there is 'a clean dark bite out of the engraving exactly where each label sits, with a soft feather, and no stroke grazes a glyph anywhere on the frame'. Deck ships with ZERO knockout plates.

entries.change: qa.py now measures text contrast at the WORST POINT of a line rather than as a box-wide mean, so type running across a graded ground is judged by its unreadable end instead of its comfortable average.
entries.trigger: The RECURRING hard fail, text against geometry plus its contrast twin, now 3 of the last 10 runs (2026-07-25, 2026-07-29, 2026-07-31), each capping the score at 6.9. The mechanism is exact. contrast_estimate() takes one background value per node, the median of non-ink pixels across the whole bounding box, and the rubric's hard-fail rule reads 'primary text contrast below 4.5 to 1 AT WORST POINT'. The machine was measuring a mean against a rule about a minimum. On this deck, whose entire premise is a lit paper sheet under one raking key, every ground is graded by construction, and the second scorer found slide 07's ballot labels and annotations bare on the lit sheet at 3.3 to 4.4 to 1 while qa.py reported zero contrast warnings on them.

entries.trigger: This run's fourth art_build defect and the only one of the five that is machine-shaped. Slide 09's 3,048-dot stipple field ran on Math.random() through five render rounds on a deck whose subject is a public RECORD, and was caught by a human running grep, not by any gate. SKILL.md has required seeded noise (AK.reseed / AK.rng, seed from the run date, 'same inputs must reproduce the same pixels') since the engine was written, and nothing enforced it. Every other check in qa.py reads ONE screenshot, so an irreproducible slide is structurally invisible to all of them: a random field is a plausible-looking field, and the defect only exists BETWEEN renders. The practical cost is that a repair round silently repaints art a pixel critic already reviewed, so the critic's note stops describing the file it was written against, and the shipped PNG cannot be rebuilt from the committed HTML.

entries.change: NEW committed technique 92, assets/js/akhachure.js, a slope-and-aspect hachure field. One short stroke per grid cell, WIDTH from the local slope of a height field, ROTATION from the local aspect, running down the line of steepest descent, strokes longer than their cell so neighbours blend, gaussian-jittered positions, each stroke bent, and the whole field redrawn several passes at low opacity with the sun azimuth varied so shadow ACCUMULATES. Three deliberate design decisions carry the point: height() is REQUIRED and has no default, so a slide can't buy the look without the data; all randomness is normally distributed off a seeded mulberry32 rather than uniform, and there is no Math.random; and the call RETURNS ITS OWN EVIDENCE as widthRatio plus named per-region probes, so a dossier declares a number before the build and a pixel critic is asked to contradict it from the render alone.
entries.trigger: Artwork craft has been the weakest scored criterion in 8 of the last 10 runs (mean 6.25, last 6.0) with two prior upgrades aimed at it and no movement. The 2026-08-02 frontier scan named the mechanism: our detail fields are parameterised by POSITION, so a declared falloff is a gradient over an otherwise-uniform texture and no reader can see it. (1) SLOPE-AND-ASPECT HACHURE SHADING, the finding that answers our standing weakness. Woodruff's sketchy-relief method is browser canvas with no dependencies: grid the height field, compute slope and aspect per cell, draw one stroke per cell with WIDTH encoding slope and ROTATION encoding aspect, make strokes longer than the cell so neighbours blend, jitter positions and bend strokes so the field reads drawn rather than stamped, then redraw the whole field several times at low opacity with the sun angle varied slightly so shadow detail ACCUMULATES. Why it matters here: our TOOTH and stipple fields are parameterised by POSITION, so a density falloff is a gradient over an otherwise identical texture, and this run proved for the second time that a reader cannot see it (the declared falloff ran in code and was invisible in every render per two pixel critics and the scorer). A hachure field is parameterised by the DATA UNDER IT, so the non-uniformity is structural rather than applied. PARKED: it wants a TECHNIQUE_LIBRARY entry with our own parameters and one trial slide judged at 432px before a director is told to reach for it. (2) HUMAN-RECOGNISABLE OBJECTS IN THE THUMB.
